business_problem: Imperial War Museums needed to make more than 20,000 hours of oral history recordings accessible despite challenges such as regional accents, military terminology, multiple languages, and inconsistent audio quality.
solution_summary: Imperial War Museums, Capgemini, and Google Cloud built a generative AI pipeline to turn a hard-to-search oral history archive into a searchable, cited research experience. Capgemini created IWM’s Google Cloud AI environment and developed a workflow that transcribes and translates audio recordings, extracts metadata, and uses Gemini 2.0 to generate interview summaries plus key people, places, and events. The application lets users search interviews through text transcripts and metadata, listen while reading synchronized transcripts, and use an “Ask a question” interface to submit natural-language queries against interviews. Responses are grounded in the source material and show citations so researchers can trust where answers came from. Prompt engineering and model tuning helped the team handle accents, multiple languages, military terminology, and inconsistent recording quality while scaling a job the museum estimated would otherwise have taken more than 20 years manually.
